name: Slovenia
summary: White, blue and red horizontal bands with the coat of arms in the upper hoist: Mount Triglav in white over two wavy blue lines, under three gold stars. Adopted on independence in 1991.
origin: The white-blue-red tricolour was first raised by Slovenes in Ljubljana in 1848, based on the colours of the Duchy of Carniola, and was used under Yugoslavia with a red star.
On independence on 25 June 1991, Slovenia removed the star and added a new coat of arms by the artist Marko Pogačnik.

symbols.name: Mount Triglav
symbols.description: A three-peaked white mountain on blue.
symbols.meaning: Triglav, Slovenia's highest peak and a national symbol.

symbols.name: Two wavy lines
symbols.description: Blue wavy lines beneath the mountain.
symbols.meaning: The Adriatic Sea and Slovenia's rivers.

symbols.name: Three stars
symbols.description: Six-pointed gold stars in a downward triangle.
symbols.meaning: From the arms of the Counts of Celje, a medieval Slovenian dynasty.

facts: Slovakia's and Russia's flags use the same three colours in the same order; Slovenia's arms sit higher and toward the hoist.
Triglav also appears on Slovenia's euro coins.
Proposals to change the flag to distinguish it from Slovakia's were considered in 2003 but not adopted.
clues: White, blue and red bands with a shield showing a three-peaked mountain and three gold stars.
Its stars come from a medieval family of counts.
Often confused with a neighbour whose name differs by a few letters.
